On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a short prep pack (POC_PreRead_v1.pdf) with agenda, pre-reads, and a one-page checklist for participants.

Hi all — quick technical checklist from my side to make the hands-on run smooth. Attaching load_test_checklist.xlsx and sample_prompts.txt (small stubs). Highlights here:

1) Environment
- Bring a laptop with stable Wi‑Fi (target 50 Mbps).
- If your security requires IP allowlisting, please send public IPs 3 business days ahead.

2) Prompt characteristics
- Max prompt length: aim for <= 1k tokens for the workshop; note outputs will add tokens.
- Please flag any prompts that include PII or proprietary keys — we'll use sanitized copies where needed.

3) Load test plan (brief)
- Baseline: 4 concurrent low‑latency streams for 10 minutes (validate routing + KV cache warming).
- Burst: increase to 12 concurrent streams in controlled 2 minute windows.
- Metrics we'll capture: p95 latency, token throughput, error rate, model fallback counts.

4) Routing note
- If you need region pinning (e.g., eu/west), tell us now so we can provision replica endpoints.

Attachments: load_test_checklist.xlsx, sample_prompts.txt

Happy to jump on a 20m pre-call with your engineering team if you want to walk through the checklist.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Looping in quick internal note (will not send externally yet):

- If Acme wants eu region testing, we need a small warm-up window and to confirm model variant (quantized vs fp16) since that affects latency.
- I recommend we default to us-west for the first run unless they specifically require eu.
- Also suggest we prepare a fallback policy in the prep pack: if p95 > 800ms for 3 consecutive samples, drop to the cheaper variant and flag in the dashboard.

Marissa — if Acme confirms eu testing, can you let procurement know? Laura — heads up for any SLA notes.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. We can do Thu, Jun 24 at 10:00 PT (that works best for our product and infra leads). Please send a calendar invite.

We reviewed the prep pack and have two short prep questions for the working session so your team can be ready:
1) Prompt review: when you say "sanitize PII", is removing names enough or do you want redaction placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED])?
2) Load test sizing: our expected token sizes are 300–800 tokens per request (outputs ~1.2x). Is the baseline plan (4 concurrent streams) sufficient to exercise routing logic for our use case?

Confirming we'll upload the 6 sample prompts to the Drive link by EOD Fri Jun 18. Also please include the shared meeting invite link and attach the pre-read to the calendar event.
